newsitem.title: GERMANY: New talks in metal sector pay row called off.
newsitem.headline: New talks in metal sector pay row called off.

text.p: New talks scheduled for next week that were aimed at finding agreement in the pay dispute within the German metal and engineering sector have been called off, the IG Metall trade union said on Monday.

IG Metall said that talks with employers originally planned to go ahead on November 19 in North Rhine-Westphalia, home to many of Germany's largest steel-producers, would now not take place. It gave no reason for the cancellation.
IG Metall announced last week that new talks were scheduled after the collapse of negotiations between it and employers in the southern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg.
The two sides had been unable to find agreement on the issue of sick pay entitlements, which employers want to cut in accordance with a new law that came into effect last month.
Employer representatives said on Monday they had not in any case considered November 19 as a definite date for the continuation of talks.

Negotiations over sick pay and other planned cuts to labour costs in the industry are now being handled at the regional level following the collapse of talks aimed at finding a national solution to the dispute.
A spokesman for the Gesamtmetall federation of metal and engineering employers said its council would be meeting this week to determine how next to proceed.
If the sick pay dispute cannot be solved in separate negotiations, it will have to be included in the regular 1997 wage round for the industry due to take place next year.
